extracted.intended_audience: general readers, fans, and researchers interested in Kevin Hart and contemporary comedy
extracted.subtask_description: A Wikipedia biography of comedian/actor Kevin Hart summarizing his life, comedic style, genres/subjects, career milestones (stand-up, film, TV), business ventures, influences, controversies, and awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genres
rubrics_metrics.description: Lists the comedic genres Hart works in: "Observational comedy; black comedy; surreal humor; insult comedy; racial humor; sarcasm; satire."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These genre labels are presented as descriptors of Hart's material and performance style; they indicate the kinds of comedic techniques and tonal registers used in his work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subjects (comic material topics)
rubrics_metrics.description: Subjects Hart covers in his comedy: "African-American culture; everyday life; human sexuality; marriage; parenting; pop culture; race relations; racism; self-deprecation."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page lists these subjects as recurring themes in Hart's routines and stand-up albums, signaling thematic criteria for evaluating the focus and voice of his comedy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comedic style / source of material
rubrics_metrics.description: Hart "found his own rhythm by delving into his insecurities and life experiences" and has said, "Because of what I do, it has to be an open book. But right now, this is a book that is being written."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This describes a creative principle: using personal life and vulnerability as the primary source of jokes and persona. It also contrasts early imitation of other comics (e.g., Chris Tucker) with developing an original voice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of personal/family narratives
rubrics_metrics.description: He "would also later talk about his mother in his stand-up routine, portraying her as a loving yet intimidating woman," and has used troubled family life (father's addiction) and admissions from his personal life in material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The biography treats revealing personal and family stories as a notable element of Hart's comedic approach — a practice that can shape audience connection and authenticity but also carries reputational risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance and commercial success metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples of success: "Hart grossed over $15 million from 'Laugh at My Pain'... the show was filmed live ... in front of 53,000 people" and he "earned an estimated $32.5 million in 2017."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Box office grosses, tour revenue, and audience size are presented as measures of a comedian's commercial impact and reach; these data points are used as benchmarks of success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mediums and formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Hart's listed media: "Stand-up, film, television" plus stand-up albums, stand-up films, TV series, voice roles, producing, hosting, and streaming specials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page emphasizes versatility across formats (live tours, recorded specials, theatrical films, TV series, streaming, voice work) as part of a modern comedian's career profile and evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Business/production ventures and platform partnerships
rubrics_metrics.description: Hart founded Laugh Out Loud (LOL) — described as "a global media and production company" — with partnerships and deals (Lionsgate, PlutoTV, Roku, Snap, Facebook, Peacock, YouTube, Sirius XM) and later became majority owner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The biography highlights production-company creation, platform deals, and brand partnerships as career-development criteria that expand creative control and distribution; awards/nominations for LOL are listed as validation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Influences
rubrics_metrics.description: Hart cites as influences: "George Carlin; Dave Chappelle; Bill Cosby; Eddie Murphy; Patrice O'Neal; Richard Pryor; Keith Robinson; Chris Rock; and Jerry Seinfeld."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listing influences functions as a stylistic benchmark: reviewers or students of comedy may use this to situate Hart's approach within comedic traditions and evaluate lineage or debt to prior performers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Controversies, public statements and reputational impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Noted incidents: Hart withdrew from hosting the 2019 Academy Awards after backlash over several homophobic tweets; he later apologized and publicly reconsidered but ultimately did not host. The page also records legal issues (DUI) and other public admissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article frames controversies and past statements as factors affecting public reception, hosting opportunities, and career decisions — implying that sensitivity, apology sincerity, and public relations management are criteria relevant to a comedian's public standing.
